summary.text: 今 means ‘now’ or ‘today,’ a temporal use attested in Shang oracle-bone writing. Its modern written structure is 亼 above 乛; the early graph’s construction and the lower mark’s meaning remain disputed.

formation.text: The current standard form is structured as 亼 above 乛. This describes its present written shape, not its ancient construction. Early oracle-bone and bronze forms are described as having a mouth-like upper part and a lower mark, sometimes omitted; the mark’s referent is disputed. One book interprets the early mark as indicating 口吟, “mouth groaning or chanting,” and proposes that temporal use displaced this meaning in Shang writing. Other accounts leave open mouth-related and wooden-clapper interpretations, so the proposed original meaning and borrowing path remain unsettled. A later Shuowen analysis divides 今 into 亼 and 乁, identifying 乁 as an ancient form of 及; this dictionary account does not settle the early graph’s construction. Separately, 今 is documented as a phonetic element in 吟, but that later role does not establish groaning or chanting as its original meaning.

components.text: 亼 is the upper unit in the current standard written form of 今. This structural identification does not establish its role in the ancient graph.
乛 is the lower unit in the current standard written form of 今. The structural record does not establish an ancient meaning or sound role for this shape.
In one disputed account, the early lower mark indicates 口吟, “mouth groaning or chanting.” This proposed graphic function does not establish that groaning was the original word written by 今.
The received Shuowen analysis names 亼 as the first part of 今. It is a later dictionary analysis and does not establish this part’s role in the early graph.

The received analysis identifies its second part as 乁, an ancient form/variant of 及. This does not make 及 an ancestor of the shape in 今. Another transcription gives 绁; the intended shape and reason for the discrepancy remain unresolved.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze forms are described with a mouth-like upper part and a lower horizontal mark, sometimes omitted. The book traces the lower mark shifting by late Shang, bending in some Western Zhou forms, then lengthening into the form inherited by seal and clerical scripts. Other accounts describe a bent lower mark in seal forms. These graphic changes do not settle what the mark represents.

The received dictionary analysis divides 今 into 亼 and 乁, identifying the latter as an ancient form of 及. Another transcription renders the second part as 绁. This later analysis does not confirm the early graph’s construction or define the modern lower unit 乛.

uncertainties.text: The early graph’s construction and lower mark are disputed. The book proposes an inverted mouth-like form with a mark indicating groaning or chanting; other proposals read a mouth-related sign or wooden clapper. The groaning/chanting analysis is not established as the original word written by 今.

The name and pronunciation of an object proposed in the mouth-related or clapper readings are not established. The pronunciation of the temporal word 今 cannot supply that missing evidence, so a sound-based borrowing account remains unproven.
A possible connection between 今 and 其 (“this”) has been proposed, but neither a historical relationship nor a semantic path is established.

The Shang oracle examples attest temporal use, while the book proposes that this use displaced an earlier groaning/chanting meaning. The cited evidence does not independently establish that earlier meaning or the proposed borrowing sequence; the individual dates of the cited inscriptions are unresolved.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone inscription; individual date unresolved
senses.text: The phrase 今夕其雨 attests the temporal meaning “now” or “today” in Shang oracle-bone writing. This is the earliest attested temporal use in the supplied evidence; whether another meaning preceded it remains unresolved.
今 is also used for “present,” “current,” and “modern era,” but the examples available here do not date how these uses developed from the earlier temporal sense.

limitations.text: The Shang temporal attestation does not establish a prior sense or a sequence of semantic development. The listed modern meanings do not date when they arose.

The proposed groaning or chanting meaning and the claim that 今 was borrowed for “now” are not independently established. No source here establishes the depicted object’s name or a sound match that would demonstrate that borrowing pathway.

relationships.text: 今 is documented as a phonetic element in 吟. In the Zhengzhang system, 今 is reconstructed as krɯm and 吟 as ŋɡrɯm: their rhyme sequences are comparable, though their initials differ. This later role does not establish 今’s proposed original word.
